issues.description: Docstring deprecation directive has a typo ('stlib' should be 'stdlib').
issues.detail: Both reviewers flagged the same typo in the .. deprecated:: 4.3 directive. Since the docstring is part of the contract and points users to the replacement API, the misspelling should be corrected while the directive is being added.

issues.description: Deprecation test does not assert stderr-redirect equivalence and matches loosely.
issues.detail: The pytest.warns match only checks the 'Please use...' suffix, and the test exercises only stdout. Since the deprecation message promises substitution by both contextlib.redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr, the test should cover the stderr path and match on a more stable token like 'deprecated'.

issues.description: Migration note should mention nesting two contextlib managers for combined stdout+stderr.
issues.detail: redirected swaps both streams in one call; contextlib provides redirect_stdout and redirect_stderr as separate context managers. Callers redirecting both must nest two contexts to preserve the original postcondition. A short note in the deprecation message or changelog would prevent silent migration regressions.

synthesis.summary: The panel accepts the PR: a small, focused deprecation of falcon.testing.redirected in favor of contextlib.redirect_stdout/redirect_stderr. The diff is clean, contract-preserving, and includes a news fragment and a warning test. Substitutability holds (streams restored on exit, including on exception). Three minor follow-ups: fix the 'stlib' docstring typo, tighten the test (loose match pattern, missing stderr path), and note in the migration guidance that combined stdout+stderr redirection requires nesting two contextlib managers.
